provenance: Raw values transcribed without rounding from the successful six-round console.table run in this session; platform details collected afterward on the same host.

platform.note: Local development host, not the remote Ubuntu Linux box. Other verification and agent work could run concurrently; no CPU affinity, network throttling, or low-end hardware emulation.

method.original: git show loads the complete original CryptoRepository source at baselineRef, SWC transpiles it, and the benchmark imports and invokes its compareBcrypt method using real bcrypt.compareSync.
method.modified: Imports the working-tree CryptoRepository and invokes its compareBcrypt method using real bcrypt.compare.
method.warmup: One four-comparison batch per version; warmup samples excluded.
method.order: Original then modified on even rounds; modified then original on odd rounds.
method.checkpointMs: Elapsed performance.now milliseconds until a setImmediate callback queued before starting the four comparisons runs.
method.totalMs: Elapsed milliseconds until all four comparison promises complete, measured before awaiting the checkpoint.
method.completedAtCheckpoint: Number of comparisons completed when the queued callback runs. Asserted to equal 4 for original and 0 for modified in every measured round.
method.assertions: Every batch must return [true, true, true, true]. No timing threshold is asserted.

invalidHashBehavior.method: Directly invoked installed bcrypt.compareSync and awaited bcrypt.compare with password="password" and the encrypted values below.

sync.name: Error
sync.message: data must be a string or Buffer and hash must be a string

async.name: Error
async.message: data and hash must be strings

invalidHashBehavior.propagation: All AuthService compareBcrypt and validateSecret/validatePinCode call sites await verification. Async bcrypt rejection propagates to the async service caller, with no catch converting it into successful authentication. Malformed string hashes return/resolve false in both APIs; invalid argument types throw/reject.

limitations: Measures event-loop responsiveness in a repository-level workload, not deployed HTTP latency or poor-network performance.
Does not demonstrate lower total CPU work; bcrypt cost and hash quality are unchanged.
Concurrent asynchronous verification uses the shared libuv worker pool and can queue or saturate CPU under load.
Timing values depend on hardware and concurrent load; the per-round completion counts are the scheduling regression check.
